rules.sentence: **Controlled and uncontrolled are exclusive**, for the value and for open: `value` or `defaultValue`, `open` or `defaultOpen`. Both is a build failure, as on Tabs and Popover.

rules.sentence: **Two alignments.** `start` and `end`; there is no `center`, `left` or `right`. The list always opens below and flips above on its own when there is no room.

rules.sentence: **An item has four fields.** `value`, `label`, `meta`, `locked`. An `icon`, `description`, `children` or `onClick` doesn't compile: choosing calls `onValueChange`, nothing else. A `locked` item has a `reason` string, and `meta` and `locked` together don't compile; nor does 0.14.0's `disabled`.

rules.sentence: **The current value must exist.** A `value` or `defaultValue` that matches no item throws a named error, rather than opening a list with nothing marked.

**It is a menu of radio items, opened from a button.** The popup is `role="menu"` named by `label`. Each item is `role="menuitemradio"`, and exactly the current one has `aria-checked="true"`. The trigger renders a `<button>`; in development, anything else throws a named error.
**The item's whole text is its name.** The accessible name includes `meta` ("Firewall, 1 new"), so what is seen is what is heard.

**Choosing closes it and returns focus.** A click, Enter or Space on an item calls `onValueChange`, closes the list and puts focus back on the trigger. Choosing the current item closes the list and returns focus too, **without** calling `onValueChange`: nothing changed.

**Opening lands on the current item, however it opens.** A click, Enter, Space, Arrow Down and Arrow Up all put focus on the current item, not the first or the last, so a keyboard user starts where they are. The next arrow key moves on from the current item, and the loop wraps from it when it is the last. A locked current item still takes focus.
**Escape, Tab and a press outside close it.** Escape returns focus to the trigger; Tab closes it and moves on through the page.
**It is non-modal.** The page keeps its scroll and its accessibility tree, and focus is not trapped: Tab leaves the list. A press outside closes it and still reaches what it landed on, as on Popover.
**A keyboard open is instant.** When the list opens or closes from the keyboard, the trigger carries `data-vela-instant` for that change, and loses it on the next pointer interaction.

**A locked item can be reached but not chosen** (DESIGN.md, *States*, Locked). It stays in the arrow-key order, so it can be read, and its reason shows where `meta` would and is heard with its name ("Archive, Needs retention on"). It has `aria-disabled="true"`, and choosing it does nothing. Icon's `lock` comes before its name, hidden from assistive technology, because the reason is already in the row (`icon.md`, *Glyphs*).

**A locked item names a setting or a policy that rules it out; a value the person's role may never have is not listed.** A permission is about who the person is; a setting or a policy is about the state of things, applies to everyone and can change. A plan limit or a fault isn't listed either. "Needs retention on." for a setting; "Set by the Data Retention policy." for a policy. The reason never says "Locked". The twin of Segmented Control's `segmented-locked-has-a-cause`.

**Names wrap in full, never truncated.** The list is where a long name is read in full, on touch too, even a name with no spaces (`customer-ingest-pipeline-eu-west-2`). When the name and its meta don't fit side by side, the meta drops under the name.
**It holds up in forced colours.** The highlighted item is the system's `Highlight` / `HighlightText` pair, and the check is drawn in `currentColor`, so it follows the row's text.
**`meta` is words, never a colour.** "1 new", "2 new", "3 open". Never a dot alone, never a coloured word.

**`meta` is never a taxonomy label.** Never "Critical", "High", "Degraded" or "Malicious". In development, a `meta` equal (ignoring case) to a Severity, Risk, Status or Verdict value or label logs a warning that names the item and the taxonomy.
